newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks end weak in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks end weak in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks predictably weakened on Thursday as new issues drove most market players to the sidelines.
The main industrial index dropped 77.55 points to close at 10,348.67 and brokers said they expected the market to drift weakly until the issues are out of the way.
"The market is coming down basically because all the money it still tied up in new issues. People are sitting on the sidelines not doing much until the issues are out of the way," one broker said.
"People are not willing to push prices and we expect the market to go down slightly and slowly until May when the new issues are out of the way," he added.

Among the day's losers on Thursday, bankers FMB FMB.ZI slid 250 cents to 4,750, Barclays cut 200 cents to 3,600, cement producer Porthold shed 50 cents to 1,700 while conglomerate TZI TZI.ZI and steel window and door-maker Radar lost 10 cents each to 1,000 and 530 respectively.
Minings were dull as the market watched a sharply lower palladium price for direction.
Gold producers Rio Tinto RTNT.ZI and Wankie Colliery traded unchanged and the mining index edged 2.2 points up to 967.74.
